name: pipe
description: pipe() creates a unidirectional pipe for interprocess communication, returning two file descriptors in an array: one for reading (pipefd[0]) and one for writing (pipefd[1]). Data written to the write end is buffered by the kernel until read from the read end.

parameters.name: pipefd
parameters.description: Array to hold the two file descriptors: pipefd[0] for the read end and pipefd[1] for the write end.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for pipe2() to modify behavior, such as O_CLOEXEC for close-on-exec, O_NONBLOCK for non-blocking I/O, or O_DIRECT for packet mode.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, sets errno, and leaves pipefd unchanged

errors.description: The per-process limit on the number of open file descriptors has been reached.
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files has been reached.
The user hard limit on memory that can be allocated for pipes has been reached.
O_NOTIFICATION_PIPE was passed in flags and support for notifications is not compiled into the kernel (for pipe2).

versions: pipe() since POSIX.1-2001; pipe2() since Linux 2.6.27, glibc 2.9
